'''Carsten Könneker''' (born February 15, 1972, in [[Leverkusen]], [[West Germany]]) is a German [[science journalism|science journalist]] and [[science communication]] researcher. From 2010 to 2019, he was editor-in-chief of ''Spektrum der Wissenschaft'', the German edition of ''[[Scientific American]]''. From 2012 to 2018, he was professor of [[science communication]] and [[science studies]] at [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]], and founding director of the German National Institute for Science Communication, [[Karlsruhe]]. From 2019 to 2022, he was one of the managing directors of the [[Klaus Tschira Foundation]].

== Education ==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=August 2023}}

Carsten Könneker studied [[German literature]], [[philosophy]] and [[art history]] (Master of Arts, [[Washington University in St. Louis]], USA, 1997) and [[physics]] (Diploma, [[University of Cologne]], Germany, 1998).<ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.spektrum.de/profil/koenneker/carsten/849154 | title=Zur Person: Prof. Dr. Carsten Könneker }}</ref> From 1998 to 2000, he wrote his dissertation on the literary, aesthetic, and political-ideological reception of [[relativity theory]] and [[quantum mechanics]] during the [[Weimar Republic]] and [[Nazi Germany]].<ref>{{cite book | url= https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-476-02773-3 | title= Dissertation published in 2001 under the title ''"Auflösung der Natur. Auflösung der Geschichte".Moderner Roman und NS-"Weltanschauung" im Zeichen der theoretischen Physik'' | date= 2001 | doi= 10.1007/978-3-476-02773-3 | last1= Könneker | first1= Carsten | isbn= 978-3-476-45262-7 }}</ref> The dissertation was supported by a scholarship from the [[German National Academic Foundation]].<ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.wmk.itz.kit.edu/1320_1325.php | title=Scholarships and awards as noted on Könneker's profile page of the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology | date=20 August 2024 }}</ref>

== Career ==
In 2000, Carsten Könneker became an editor at ''Spektrum der Wissenschaft'', the German edition of ''[[Scientific American]]'', which later became part of [[Springer Nature]]'s [[Nature Portfolio]]. In this position, he played a key role in the development of the popular science magazine ''Gehirn & Geist'', founded in 2002, which provides interdisciplinary coverage of [[neuroscience]], [[psychology]], [[artificial intelligence]], and [[philosophy of mind]], and which was later, since 2004, published in the U.S. as an adapted edition under the title ''[[Scientific American Mind]].'' Also in 2004, Könneker became editor-in-chief of ''Gehirn & Geist.''<ref>{{cite web | url=https://kress.de/news/beitrag/42504-perso-spektrum.html | title=Perso spektrum }}</ref> In 2010, he became editor-in-chief of ''Spektrum der Wissenschaft'' as well as its online platform ''Spektrum.de''.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://kress.de/news/beitrag/100875-koenneker-kommt-2011-fuer-breuer.html | title=Könneker kommt 2011 für Breuer }}</ref> In 2011, Könneker founded ''Spektrum Neo'' as a children's science magazine in the Spektrum portfolio.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://kress.de/news/beitrag/108045-ende-august-startet-quot-spektrum-neo-quot.html | title=Ende August startet "Spektrum neo" }}</ref> He received the Werner-und-Inge-Grüter-Prize for Science Communication for that magazine in 2012.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://grueter-stiftung.de/preistraeger-2012/ | title=Preisträger 2012 }}</ref>

Also in 2012, in addition to his editorial work, Könneker was appointed full professor for [[science communication]] and [[science studies]] at [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]] (KIT),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wmk.itz.kit.edu/1320_1325.php|title=KIT - Department für Wissenschaftskommunikation - Team|first=W. M. K.|last=Karlsruhe|date=March 29, 2023|website=www.wmk.itz.kit.edu}}</ref> where he helped establish the research field Science of Science Communication at that institution. He was also the founding scientific director of the German National Institute for Science Communication in [[Karlsruhe]], jointly funded by KIT and the [[Klaus Tschira Foundation]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.kit.edu/kit/pi_2022_038_wissenschaftskommunikation-zehn-jahre-nawik.php | title=KIT - das KIT - Medien - Presseinformationen - Archiv Presseinformationen - Wissenschaftskommunikation: Zehn Jahre NaWik | date=15 February 2023 }}</ref>

[[File:Actor model of science communication by Carsten Könneker.png|thumb|Actor model of science communication by Carsten Könneker (first published in 2016)|alt=|320x320px]]

Könneker is the originator of the actor model of [[science communication]], which he first published in 2016. He is also known for his examination of the effects of technological and media developments on science communication: in 2013, Könneker argued in the journal ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'', that the advent of [[social media]] at that time represented an epochal development for [[science communication]] as well, as it opened up new opportunities for researchers in particular to engage in external science communication in a self-mediated way.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Public Science 2.0—Back to the Future|first1=Carsten|last1=Könneker|first2=Beatrice|last2=Lugger|date=October 4, 2013|journal=Science|volume=342|issue=6154|pages=49–50|doi=10.1126/science.1245848|pmid=24092719 |bibcode=2013Sci...342...49K |s2cid=206552338 |doi-access=free}}</ref> Könneker later addressed the development and widespread availability of [[artificial intelligence]] based on large language models for science, science communication and the interest-driven shaping of public discourse. He postulated the emergence of entirely new multimodal exploitation chains for scientific content and analyzed opportunities, e.g. for more precise target group engagement and for more educational equity, but also risks due to incorrect automated information, targeted disinformation and misuse.<ref>{{Cite news|url= https://www.faz.net/aktuell/wissen/wissenschaftskommunikation-worauf-es-beim-einsatz-von-ki-ankommt-19230018.html|title=Wenn der Rechner das Wort ergreift|first=Carsten|last=Könneker|access-date=2024-04-12 |trans-title=When the Computer Takes the Floor |work=Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung|language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ssir.org/articles/entry/science-communication-artificial-intelligence|title=The Challenge of Science Communication in the Age of AI|website=ssir.org|language=en |access-date=2024-04-12}}</ref>

In 2019, Könneker became one of two managing directors of the [[Klaus Tschira Foundation]], one of Europe's largest private foundations dedicated to science and science communication, a post he held until 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://klaus-tschira-stiftung.de/meldungen/neue-geschaeftsfuehrung/|title=Klaus Tschira Stiftung künftig mit neuer Doppelspitze|website=Klaus Tschira Stiftung}}</ref>
